proposal.comment: [Playbook] TrueLink's indemnity covers only its own breach of the Agreement, so an infringement claim against us arising from the Interface (which TrueLink owns and does not warrant as non-infringing) would fall on Client. We have added the standard IP-infringement, breach-of-law, data-incident and gross negligence/wilful misconduct prongs.

ops.newText: claim arising out of (i) any breach by TrueLink of this Agreement or any failure by TrueLink in the performance of any of its obligations or agreements hereunder; (ii) any allegation that the Interface, the Hosting Services, the Support Services or any deliverable provided hereunder infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right of a third party; (iii) TrueLink's violation of applicable law or any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content, Credit Data or Client Proprietary Information caused by TrueLink; or (iv) TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct.
ops.oldText: claim arising out of any breach by TrueLink of this Agreement or any failure by TrueLink in the performance of any of its obligations or agreements hereunder.

proposal.summary: Add IP infringement, breach of law, data-breach and gross negligence prongs to TrueLink's indemnity.

quote: TrueLink shall indemnify and hold Client harmless, its affiliates, directors, officers, employees, agents and licensors harmless from and against all claims, actions, expenses, losses, and liabilities, including reasonable attorneys' fees, arising from or relating to any
rationale: TrueLink's indemnity is limited to claims arising from its own breach or performance failure and does not cover third-party IP infringement by the Interface or hosted site (there is no non-infringement warranty either), nor its breach of law, data incidents or gross negligence — so it fails the fallback, while Client's indemnity in 12(a) is unusually broad. We added the standard IP, breach-of-law, data-incident and gross negligence/wilful misconduct prongs.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 8(d) lets TrueLink distribute, license, resell and exploit our borrowers' Credit Data; we can only grant a licence to use that data to provide the services, and we retain all rights in Client Content, Credit Data and Client's Intellectual Property.

ops.newText: Client hereby grants to TrueLink a nonexclusive, worldwide, royalty-free right and license to use, upload, display, copy, transmit and store Credit Data solely as necessary to provide the Hosting Services and Support Services to Client, subject to the limitations set forth in and in accordance with the Non-Competition Agreement. TrueLink shall not distribute, disseminate, license, resell or otherwise exploit Credit Data for any other purpose, and Client retains all right, title and interest in and to Client Content, Credit Data and Client's Intellectual Property.
ops.oldText: Client hereby grants to TrueLink the nonexclusive worldwide right and license to use, distribute, disseminate, license, resell, exploit, upload, display, copy and store Credit Data subject to the limitations set forth in and in accordance with the Non-Competition Agreement.

proposal.summary: Narrow the Credit Data licence to service provision and confirm Client retains all rights in its content and data.

quote: Client hereby grants to TrueLink the nonexclusive worldwide right and license to use, distribute, disseminate, license, resell, exploit, upload, display, copy and store Credit Data subject to the limitations set forth in and in accordance with the Non-Competition Agreement.
rationale: Section 8(d) grants TrueLink rights to distribute, license, resell and exploit Credit Data — data of our borrowers and loan applicants — which goes beyond a service-provision licence and cuts against our position that Customer retains all rights in its data. Ownership elsewhere is acceptable (TrueLink keeps the Interface under 2(d); Client keeps its domains and Client Content under Section 13, and Client's IP and service results are Client Proprietary Information under Section 10). We narrowed the grant to what is needed to provide the services and confirmed Client's retained rights.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The cap in Section 12 protects TrueLink only and leaves Client's liability unlimited; our position is a mutual 12-month fee cap with a mutual exclusion of indirect damages. We have mirrored TrueLink's own cap language for Client rather than reopening the scope of TrueLink's cap, and confirm that Client's payment obligations, and each party's gross negligence, wilful misconduct, confidentiality breaches and indemnification obligations, sit outside the cap.

ops.text: IN NO EVENT SHALL CLIENT'S LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO THIS AGREEMENT (OTHER THAN CLIENT'S OBLIGATION TO PAY FEES DUE UNDER SECTION 5, OR A BREACH RESULTING FROM CLIENT'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT) EXCEED THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD. NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO THIS AGREEMENT.

proposal.summary: Make the liability cap mutual by adding a matching cap on Client's liability and a mutual consequential-damages exclusion.

quote: IN NO EVENT SHALL TRUELINK'S LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11 THIS AGREEMENT (OTHER THAN DUE TO A BREACH RESULTING FROM TRUELINK'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT) EXCEED THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD.
rationale: The only cap is one-way: it limits TrueLink to 12 months' hosting/support compensation while Client's liability (including under the very broad Section 12(a) indemnity) is unlimited, which is walk-away territory under our playbook. There is also no mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages and no statement that Client's payment obligations sit outside the cap. We added a mirrored cap on Client plus a mutual consequential-damages exclusion, deliberately leaving the scope of TrueLink's own cap untouched.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 15 allows affiliate assignments but blocks a transfer to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets; we need the usual successor carve-out on notice and a "not unreasonably withheld" standard for other assignments.

ops.newText: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate or, upon written notice to the other party, to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of the assigning party's assets. No change of control of Client shall give TrueLink any right to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement.
ops.oldText: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.

proposal.summary: Add an M&A/successor carve-out, a reasonableness standard on consent, and confirm no change-of-control right for TrueLink.

quote: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
rationale: Section 15 is mutual and allows affiliate transfers, but it has no M&A/successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard on consent, so TrueLink could block a transfer on our merger or sale of assets — short of the fallback. We added a successor carve-out on notice, a "not unreasonably withheld" standard, and confirmation that a Client change of control gives TrueLink no termination or re-pricing right.

quote: TrueLink hereby grants to Client a non-exclusive license to use the Interface
rationale: No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binds Client; the licence is non-exclusive and Section 2(a) confirms Client may source similar software and services elsewhere. Nothing in Sections 2, 5 or 8 requires us to host or procure exclusively through TrueLink.

quote: Invoices will be paid within 15 days of receipt.
rationale: No liquidated damages, penalty, late-fee or termination-charge payable by Client appears in the Agreement, including in Section 5 or the spam provisions of Section 7 (breach there gives TrueLink only technical and equitable remedies). The monthly minimum fees in Section 5 are addressed under MINCOMMIT rather than double-flagged here.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The grant runs to Client alone; our licences must cover affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, otherwise ordinary use by group companies and outsourced staff is a breach.

ops.newText: TrueLink hereby grants to Client, its affiliates and its contractors acting on Client's behalf a non-exclusive license to use the Interface in the ordinary course of its business
ops.oldText: TrueLink hereby grants to Client a non-exclusive license to use the Interface in the ordinary course of its business

proposal.summary: Extend the licence to Client's affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf.

quote: TrueLink hereby grants to Client a non-exclusive license to use the Interface in the ordinary course of its business of the origination, underwriting, processing and funding of consumer finance receivables in accordance with this Agreement.
rationale: The grant runs to Client only; affiliates are not covered and Section 8(c) limits access to Client's own officers, employees and approved agents, with no path to add group companies, so the clause falls short of the fallback (affiliates covered on notice). The licence is at least not revocable at will and runs for the term, and Exhibit A sites can be amended by notice. We inserted affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf into the grant.

quote: Client is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system, design, formula, procedure or trade secret to provide software and services similar to the ones provided by TrueLink hereunder
rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction binds Client; Section 2(a) expressly preserves our freedom to build, buy or license competing software, subject only to standard IP and confidentiality limits. We note Section 8(d) refers to a separate Non-Competition Agreement, which should be reviewed on its own terms but imposes nothing in this document.

quote: TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: Section 14 gives Client an unconditional right to terminate on notice, effective at the end of the following month (roughly 30–60 days), with no early-termination fee, and TrueLink has no convenience exit (its termination rights in Section 13 are breach-triggered). This meets or betters our preferred position; we note only that there is no express pro-rata refund mechanic, though fees are invoiced monthly in arrears.

quote: Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge
rationale: There is no audit, inspection or usage-verification right running against Client anywhere in the Agreement (a full-text search returns no audit language); Section 6 runs the other way, giving Client documentation and dispute rights. This meets our preferred position, so no redline.

quote: This Agreement shall be governed, construed and interpreted in accordance with the laws of the State of California (without respect to principles of conflicts of law).
rationale: California law with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in California sits at our accepted fallback (California law and courts), and there is no arbitration. We note only that venue is San Luis Obispo County, TrueLink's home county rather than our preferred forum — acceptable, so no redline.

quote: TrueLink agrees that the costs for any Hosting Services will not increase for a period of one year from the date of this Agreement and that rates charged for Hosting Services will not exceed that charged by TrueLink to any other party.
rationale: The only MFN runs in our favour — TrueLink's hosting rates may not exceed those charged to any other customer. No obligation requires Client to extend best terms to TrueLink, so no redline.

quote: Client will pay TrueLink's fees for requested Hosting Services and Support Services pursuant to the schedule of charges set forth on Exhibits "A" and "B" attached hereto, (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services).
rationale: Section 5 imposes a monthly fee floor rather than a multi-year take-or-pay, and Client can exit that exposure at any time under Section 14 (effective the end of the following month) with no penalty, which sits within the fallback. We note for the commercial team that the minimum amounts are still blank and that Section 6 excludes those minimums from our documentation and dispute rights — points to settle before signature rather than a playbook deviation.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

rationale: A full-text search for solicitation, hiring and inducement language returns only the unsolicited-e-mail provisions in Section 7; neither the Client covenants in Section 8 nor the confidentiality provisions in Section 10 contain a non-solicit or no-hire binding Client. This matches our preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer).

quote: This Agreement shall renew automatically thereafter for successive one year periods until terminated pursuant to Section 12 herein or unless either Client or TrueLink deliver to the other written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year.
rationale: Renewals are 12 months with a mutual 30-day non-renewal window, which meets our preferred position; Client can in any event exit under Section 14 at any time. We note two minor points not worth redlining: there is no Vendor renewal reminder and no cap on renewal price increases beyond the first-year freeze and the MFN in Section 6 (the cross-reference to "Section 12" in Section 13 should read Section 14).

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 13 puts the whole exit burden on Client (finding a name server and new hosting environment) with no obligation on TrueLink to return our data or help migrate; we have added our standard transition-assistance, data-return and deletion language.

ops.text: Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall (a) at Client's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at TrueLink's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return to Client all Client Content, Credit Data and other Client data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance, data return and deletion obligations on termination.

quote: If Client decides to discontinue its Hosting Service, Client is responsible for arranging for a new name server within 30 days. In case of discontinued Service, Client shall retain full ownership of all domains associated with Client and Client Content. If Client decides to discontinue Hosting Service, Client is responsible for arranging for a new hosting environment within 60 days.
rationale: Exit obligations run only against Client (arranging a new name server and hosting environment); TrueLink owes no transition assistance, no return or export of Client Content, Credit Data or backups, and no deletion certification, which is a deviation for a hosting vendor. We inserted our standard six-month transition assistance, 30-day data return and certified deletion language into the termination provisions; 90 days of assistance is our fallback.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 9 warrants only Y2K readiness and Section 12 disclaims everything else, so we have no conformance warranty or remedy for the hosted Interface. We have added the standard workmanlike/conformance warranty with a repair-or-refund remedy; we can accept the 90-day (rather than 12-month) period as a fallback.

ops.text: TrueLink further represents and warrants that (i) the Hosting Services and Support Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards, and (ii) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, the Interface and each deliverable provided under Section 4 will conform in all material respects to its documentation and specifications. Client's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at TrueLink's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming services or deliverable. The disclaimer set forth in Section 12 does not limit the express warranties in this Section 9.

proposal.summary: Add a performance and conformance warranty with a repair/re-perform/refund remedy, carved out of the disclaimer.

quote: EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT, TRUELINK DISCLAIMS ANY AND ALL EXPENSES WARRANTIES, WARRANTIES OF FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FOR ANY MATTER RELATING TO THE ACCURACY OR COMPLETENESS, OR TIMING OF TRANSMISSION OF ANY DATA SUBMITTED THROUGH THE INTERFACE OR TO OR FROM THE WEB SITE.
rationale: TrueLink's only express warranties are Y2K-readiness (Section 9); there is no conformance-to-documentation warranty and no repair/re-perform/refund remedy, and everything else is disclaimed in Section 12, with Section 11 offering only a self-referential standard of care. That fails the fallback, so we inserted the standard workmanlike and 90-day conformance warranty with remedies, expressly carved out of the disclaimer.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no insurance covenant even though TrueLink hosts our site and handles borrower credit data; we have inserted our standard CGL/E&O/cyber requirement, and can drop to E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M if needed.

ops.text: 31. INSURANCE. TrueLink shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where TrueLink processes Client Content or Credit Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. TrueLink shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

proposal.summary: Insert a standard vendor insurance covenant in the general provisions.

quote: 30. FORCE MAJEURE. TrueLink will be excused from delays in performing or from failing to perform its obligations under this Agreement to the extent the delays or failures result from causes beyond the reasonable control or TrueLink.
rationale: The Agreement contains no insurance covenant at all, yet TrueLink hosts our Web Site and processes borrower credit data — walk-away territory under this rule. We inserted a short insurance section (CGL, E&O and cyber, certificates on request) in the general provisions; E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M is our fallback.
